newsitem.title: USA: Two Houston officials indicted for corruption.
newsitem.headline: Two Houston officials indicted for corruption.

text.p: Two Houston city councilman were indicted Wednesday with four other people on federal charges of public corruption resulting from an FBI sting operation conducted in 1995.
U.S. prosecutor Mike Attanasio said the six people face charges ranging from conspiracy to bribery, which carry punishment of up to 10 years in prison.
The indicted included City Councilmen Mike Yarbrough and John Castillo and former Councilmen Ben Reyes and John Peavy, who were on the council at the time of the sting.

The FBI operation consisted of setting up a false company whose frontmen offered money to council members to help ensure they would get part of a contract to build a hotel at the city's convention centre.
"These are serious offences, serious violations that involve public corruption," Attanasio told reporters.

Also indicted were former city council aide Ross Allyn and Port of Houston commissioner Betty Maldonado, who earlier said she was hired by the phony company to set up meetings with the city councilmembers.
Her attorney, Dick DeGuerin, speaking to reporters outside the federal courthouse, said he was certain his client would not be convicted once a jury heard her story.
"They'll not only acquit Betty Maldonado, they'll be ready to lynch the FBI," he said.
